title: Anki Miner Android AnkiDroid callback payloads
$comment: Every callback is synchronous and returns an envelope. Responses repeat runId/requestId; media and note results are positionally aligned with requests. verifyTarget validates model/fields before creating the deck and its ordered fieldNames[0] is the duplicate identity for the run. Duplicate scans are bounded candidate-key lookups, never full-model scans. Kotlin returns raw provider first fields and Python alone applies the desktop duplicate normalizer. Duplicate baselines and known-vocabulary cursors are opaque, run-bound Kotlin state, not client-echoed provider IDs. Every card and dictionary asset is Python-stat-gated at 64 MiB and streamed through cancellable SHA-1/SHA-256 hashing; each media callback is bounded to 50 assets and 64 MiB total. Kotlin must stream sourcePath into a private bounded snapshot, reject unless its byte count and SHA-256 exactly match the expected values, then expose only that snapshot to AnkiDroid. A stored result means the provider-returned filename has a safely proven postcondition; blind retry after an uncertain insert is forbidden. preferredName is the safe extensionless prefix required by AnkiDroid addMediaFromUri; requestedFilename preserves the exact direct-fallback basename; actualFilename is a raw basename, never [sound:] or markup, and Python rewrites marked dictionary HTML to the provider-returned name. Runtime validation additionally enforces aggregate duplicate-hit and note UTF-8/item/envelope budgets, provider-name relationships and collisions, unique positive note IDs, and strict notAttempted suffixes with top-level errors.

canonicalNonEmptyString.$comment: Runtime validation additionally enforces NFC and rejects every Unicode category-C code point.

filename.$comment: Runtime validation additionally enforces NFC, bare-basename semantics, and rejects every Unicode category-C code point.

mediaBasename.$comment: Exact media basename used by the direct-name fallback. Runtime validation rejects slash, backslash, dot-segments, and every Unicode category-C code point; valid Yomitan names may contain quotes, brackets, spaces, and non-NFC text.

allOf.$comment: A callback returns the raw filename, never Anki field markup.

firstField.$comment: Exact built first-field value. Kotlin computes AnkiDroid's field checksum from this value and returns the bounded raw provider hits. The key is an opaque Python-normalized identity; Kotlin must not normalize or compare against it.

key.$comment: Opaque Python-normalized identity included for positional auditability. Kotlin must not normalize or interpret it.

firstField.$comment: Exact verified model first field whose AnkiDroid checksum selects the provider note-ID snapshot. The baseline IDs remain private Kotlin state behind baselineToken.

occurrence.$comment: Zero-based ordered probe occurrence. Values in createNotes are unique and strictly increasing; Kotlin verifies the candidate at each occurrence against the token-bound occurrence map, preventing replay or fan-out of repeated candidates.

knownVocabularyScope.$comment: Kotlin scans at most maxScannedNotes notes per page and maxTotalScannedNotes across the complete stable provider traversal. An excluded deck excludes the entire note when any of its cards is in that deck or a descendant; a parent exclusion therefore covers all subdecks. cursor is null on the first page and otherwise exactly the prior nextCursor. Kotlin retains the traversal snapshot and immutable run/scope/ordinal/total binding behind each opaque one-use token; tokens expire when consumed, on terminal completion, on error, or when the run is cancelled/terminated. A cursor from another run or scope, a replay, and continuation at the total ceiling fail closed. Kotlin must fail rather than truncate or skip an oversized first field.

token.$comment: Opaque, one-use provider continuation capability bound to the originating run, immutable scan scope, next ordinal, retained stable traversal snapshot, and cumulative scanned-note count. Runtime validation caps encoded UTF-8 length at 1024 bytes.

duplicateScope.$comment: firstFieldName must exactly equal fieldNames[0] from this run's verified model snapshot. Kotlin retains the complete scoped candidate-ID baseline behind a fresh opaque baselineToken; the token and its candidate/scope/model binding expire when consumed, when the run terminates or is cancelled, or when bounded provider state is evicted by rejecting the request.

occurrences.$comment: Ordered occurrence-to-candidate indexes for the original Python batch. This preserves repeated candidate multiplicity while candidates remains a bounded unique lookup set.

baselineToken.$comment: Fresh, opaque and run-bound. Kotlin alone retains the complete provider note-ID baseline and accepts this token for at most one createNotes callback.

rawFirstFieldHits.$comment: Outer entries are positionally aligned with duplicateScope.candidates. Kotlin queries note IDs plus raw first fields by the checksum of each exact firstField and, when deckName is non-null, retains only notes with a card in that exact deck (never children). Note IDs are unique within each bucket. Kotlin must fail instead of truncating when any requested limit would be exceeded; Python validates every limit again and owns all HTML/media/entity/NFC/whitespace normalization. Provider note IDs never round-trip through createNotes; Kotlin binds them privately to baselineToken.

preferredName.$comment: Safe extensionless addMediaFromUri prefix; dictionary media uses a deterministic digest alias.

requestedFilename.$comment: Exact full basename required by a direct-name media fallback. Card assets use safe content-addressed names; dictionary assets preserve valid Yomitan basenames.

storeMediaResult.$comment: notAttempted rows form a strict suffix and require a top-level error. Callback-wide anki.error is valid only before this callback mutates provider state. A provider-wide stop after any attempted mutation must use this aligned result shape so Python retains every known stored filename. Retry is allowed only when Kotlin proves no provider mutation occurred or verifies the desired postcondition; an uncertain insert is non-retryable.

createNotesLimits.$comment: All byte limits are exact encoded UTF-8 counts. note content is the sum of field-name, field-value and tag bytes. envelope is the complete canonical bridge JSON envelope. Kotlin validates every declared constant before parsing provider-bound values and rejects rather than truncating.

createNotesRequest.$comment: Kotlin atomically consumes baselineToken only when its run/model/verified firstFieldName/candidate/scope binding exactly matches this request. It resolves every candidate's scoped checksum note IDs before inserting any note. A note is duplicate iff that immutable pre-insert snapshot contains an ID absent from the private baseline. maxTotalNoteIds counts the union of IDs across candidates. Kotlin fails rather than truncating on every declared limit and must never add IDs created by this same request to the snapshot, so repeated same-expression notes in exactDeck mode are all created when no external ID appeared. A new checksum collision may safely false-positive; a new external note must never false-negative. The exactDeck deckName must equal the top-level target deck at runtime. Callback-wide anki.error is valid only before any provider mutation. After a possible mutation Kotlin returns an aligned result, preserves every known inserted noteId, and uses a non-retryable uncertain row when commit state cannot be proven. Blind write retry is forbidden.

failedNote.$comment: The provider proved that this note was not committed. This row ends attempts; every later row is notAttempted.

committedFailedNote.$comment: The note was inserted and its ID is known, but a required post-insert routing or verification step failed. Python retains noteId. The top-level error is non-retryable and every later row is notAttempted.

uncertainNote.$comment: A provider mutation may have committed but no safe note ID/postcondition can be proven. The top-level error code is post_commit_uncertain with retryable=false and every later row is notAttempted.

createNotesResult.$comment: Rows are request-aligned. failed, committedFailed, uncertain, or notAttempted requires a top-level error and ends attempts; notAttempted is a strict suffix. Any known created/committed note IDs are retained. An error after any provider mutation is never retryable. Cancellation observed after a possible commit is post_commit_uncertain, not a clean cancelled result.
